messages:
maria: noticing a p99 spike in SIN POP starting ~08:22 UTC, looks like token latency from hosted models increased from 45ms to 420ms for a few minutes. Alerting here.
ops-bot: Incident detected: sin-pop-high-latency - 08:24 UTC - auto page sent to oncall.
maria: attaching short tail logs, not seeing obvious CPU or GPU saturation. batch sizes dropped to 1 briefly.
kevin: can you paste a slice of runtime logs? I want to see kernel selection events and any fallback reasons.
maria: log snippet: 
```
[08:22:07] kernel_selector: chosen kernel=fast_attn_v2 (latency_est=12ms)
[08:22:09] kernel_selector: fallback->compat_kernel due to metadata lookup timeout (err=EAI_AGAIN)
[08:22:09] batching: flush_reason=policy_timeout in_flight=3 -> effective_batch=1
[08:22:10] kvcache: miss_ratio jump 2.3%->18.7% (ttl: 30s)
```
jin: EAI_AGAIN is DNS related. SIN POP has had some noisy responses from the shared resolver yesterday. We saw transient SERVFAIL/rate-limit behavior from the provider's LDNS.
kevin: interesting — our runtime fetches model shard metadata and kernel capability probes via hostnames during cold-paths. If getaddrinfo blocks, the kernel selector falls back to compatibility kernels (slower) and also the batching heuristic times out, so batches flush. That would explain p99 blowup + lower throughput.
samira: kvcache miss climb could be because metadata lookups failing cause codepaths to rebuild caches or mark entries stale. Do we have profiler traces?
maria: uploaded perf trace link (internal) — top shows wakeups around name resolution syscalls and slow socket connect. Quick strace: 
```
getaddrinfo("meta.redwood.internal", ...) = -1 EAI_AGAIN (Temporary failure in name resolution) <timeout 2500ms>
connect(12, ...) = -1 ETIMEDOUT (Connection timed out) <timeout 1200ms>
```
kevin: profiling from runtime: kernel_probe_count increased 5x, compat_kernel_time accounted for +340ms p99 delta. Also CPU shows user time spent in resolver glue.
jin: dug a little deeper: dig +short @provider-ldns meta.redwood.internal sometimes returns empty and occasionally TCP fallback takes 2s. Provider confirmed they're applying rate-limits to our queries after a noisy client was misconfigured.
maria: so causal chain: LDNS rate-limit -> getaddrinfo timeouts -> kernel_selector triggers fallback + batching timeout -> kvcache churn -> p99 spike. Makes sense.
kevin: short-term mitigation options: 1) change runtime to prefer cached kernel metadata and avoid blocking lookup on the hot path (non-blocking resolver), 2) pin kernel selection to last-known-good for X minutes when resolver errors exceed threshold, 3) tweak batching heuristic to wait slightly longer when kernel fallback observed so it can coalesce. Which do we want now?
samira: ops asks for a quick patch to reduce impact until provider fix. Option 2 is lowest-risk. We can implement a hotfix: if resolver errors > 3 in 60s, use pinned kernel and increase batch wait from 5ms->25ms for that POP.
kevin: will open PR for kernel-pin + batch-wait bump, add feature flag. I have a small change ready, will run unit + canary.
maria: can we also add local caching of DNS on the POP (dnsmasq) as a fallback? That would stop provider rate-limits from affecting runtime directly.
jin: yes we'll provision dnsmasq on SIN edge now, bind it to 127.0.0.1 and set /etc/resolv.conf precedence. That should cut observed DNS latency to <10ms for repeated queries.
deploy-bot: request approved by samira for emergency canary deploy to sin-pop. CI: green. Rolling canary: 2 instances -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%.
kevin: canary logs look good, kernel fallbacks dropped to zero, effective batch sizes returned to median 8, p99 fell back to baseline.
maria: leaving this thread open until dnsmasq / provider confirm. Add followups: - postmortem if provider rate-limits persist - add non-blocking resolver path in runtime (kevin) - add metric for resolver_error_rate per POP (maria)
samira: noted, I'll update incident tracker and schedule a retro with infra & networking. :thumbsup:
jin: provider says they're rolling rate-limit fixes. We'll still keep dnsmasq as a durable mitigation.
ops-bot: Incident sin-pop-high-latency resolved at 08:40 UTC.
maria: nice work all — saved a lot of p99s. Marking this as monitoring->observability tickets for long-term fixes. :eyes:
